conflicts.quote: **`absent-is-not-none`** — three closed absence classes must remain distinguishable in types / store outcomes all the way to the research consumer: **`no session book`** (never archived for that identity) ≠ **empty / pruned intraday ring** ≠ **archive store disabled or unreadable**.
conflicts.why: PM rule 6 and UX's closed term set require four separately observable outcomes (miss ≠ empty ring ≠ not-storing/disabled ≠ unreadable/corrupt). My own isolation table already splits disabled-open from corrupt-body; the binding restatement's 'three' OR collapses the last two and understates the store-outcome surface peers bind.
conflicts.proposal: Bind four research outcomes end-to-end: `no session book` ≠ `empty 48-ring` ≠ `session archive not storing` / disabled ≠ `session book unreadable` — keep the isolation-table split; retire the 'three classes' restatement.

conflicts.why: Product closed rule and architect store outcomes require four distinguishable classes: `no session book` ≠ empty 48-ring ≠ disabled/not-storing ≠ unreadable/corrupt. Folding disabled and unreadable into one of “three absences” (even with an and/or string pair) lets an operator confuse “configure/enable the store” with “repair a corrupt body,” which is the same honesty failure `absent-is-not-none` forbids.
conflicts.proposal: Keep four mandatory-distinct operator outcomes: use `session archive not storing` only when the archive is disabled/unavailable, and `session book unreadable: <reason>` only when an identity exists but cannot be read — never as interchangeable labels for one shared state.

conflicts.quote: **`review` owns** absence of trader UI (AC-15), not raising the 48 cap (AC-19), program #2–#7 not absorbed (AC-20/21), operator-without-trader-UI check (AC-22), and the explicit “authorizes: nothing” research framing (AC-23).
conflicts.why: Trader-UI silence is negative space. A human review cannot reliably notice what is absent across Landing, Ticker, Settings, Ask-AI, Scanner, Positions, and shell nav after an unrelated change lands a badge, toast, or Settings row. That is exactly the silently-regressing class risk-based-verify assigns to `test`. Bundling AC-15 with AC-22 under `review` also conflates two different risks: absence of trader chrome (must be asserted) vs presence of an operator path (visible/intentional).
conflicts.proposal: Keep AC-15 ship-blocking; mark Verify by **test** (structural `apps/dashboard` empty-diff / no new trader route affordance), matching UX-1/UX-2. Leave AC-19/20/21/22/23 as **review**. No DOM harness required — file/route negative assertion is enough.

conflicts.quote: **UX / interface (via synthesizer later)** will key session list/load on **`(symbol, et_date)`**, not on ring `as_of` alone — provenance `source_as_of` may be shown but is not the session identity.
conflicts.why: I accept `(symbol, et_date)` as identity and that provenance is not the key. I reject optional provenance under the rest of Architect's own position: first-wins plus eligibility that does not gate on RTH means the archived body can be a pre/post-RTH morning book while operator vocabulary and the BRIEF still say "ET trading session." If `source_as_of` is only "may" be shown, research copy can assert a session/RTH meaning the bytes do not support — my defining failure mode.
conflicts.proposal: Keep identity `(symbol, et_date)` and first-wins if PM accepts them. Make `source_as_of` / `archived from capture at <UTC>` mandatory on every successful operator session-book read (still not the identity). If product wants the noun to mean RTH close only, change eligibility or conflict policy instead of leaving provenance optional.
